title: The Mechanistic Study of Melatonin Regulation of p16Ink4a and Oct4 in Anti-Cellular Senescence.
authors: Xu, Yang; Zhang, Cong; Wang, Li; Chen, Xiaoyu
journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
one_liner_zh: 该文研究褪黑素通过VDR调控p16/OCT4抗衰老机制，涉及蛋白-蛋白互作与分子对接，但核心是蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Melatonin is a multifunctional indole hormone with established roles in anti-aging and tissue regeneration. Although it has been shown to modulate key senescence-associated markers such as p16Ink4a (p16) and OCT4, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. MC3T3-E1 cells were treated with melatonin to evaluate its effects on p16 and OCT4 expression using Western blot and RT-qPCR. Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) and molecular docking were employed to investigate protein-protein interactions and structural binding patterns. VDR knockdown experiments were performed to assess functional causality. In addition, osteogenic differentiation was evaluated in bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) using alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and Alizarin Red S (ARS) staining. Melatonin significantly downregulated p16 and upregulated OCT4 expression without affecting cell viability. ITC analysis revealed that melatonin does not directly bind to p16 or OCT4, but both proteins interact with the vitamin D receptor (VDR) with moderate affinity. Molecular docking further supported stable binding conformations between VDR and p16/OCT4. Functionally, VDR knockdown disrupted the balance of p16 and OCT4 expression and impaired osteogenic differentiation, as evidenced by decreased ALP activity and reduced mineralized nodule formation. These findings identify VDR as a critical mediator of melatonin signalling and reveal a novel VDR-centered regulatory axis linking senescence and stemness pathways. This mechanism provides new insights into the anti-senescence and pro-regenerative effects of melatonin and suggests potential therapeutic strategies for aging-related diseases such as osteoporosis.
abstract_zh: 褪黑素是一种多功能吲哚类激素，在抗衰老和组织再生中具有公认的作用。尽管已证明其能调节关键的衰老相关标志物，如p16Ink4a（p16）和OCT4，但其潜在分子机制仍未完全阐明。用褪黑素处理MC3T3-E1细胞，通过Western blot和RT-qPCR评估其对p16和OCT4表达的影响。采用等温滴定量热法（ITC）和分子对接研究蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用及结构结合模式。进行VDR敲低实验以评估功能因果关系。此外，在骨髓来源间充质干细胞（BMSCs）中，使用碱性磷酸酶（ALP）和茜素红S（ARS）染色评估成骨分化。褪黑素显著下调p16并上调OCT4表达，且不影响细胞活力。ITC分析显示，褪黑素不直接结合p16或OCT4，但两种蛋白均与维生素D受体（VDR）以中等亲和力相互作用。分子对接进一步支持VDR与p16/OCT4之间的稳定结合构象。功能上，VDR敲低破坏了p16和OCT4表达的平衡，并损害成骨分化，表现为ALP活性降低和矿化结节形成减少。这些发现将VDR确定为褪黑素信号传导的关键介导因子，并揭示了一个以VDR为中心的新调控轴，连接衰老和干性通路。该机制为褪黑素的抗衰老和促再生效应提供了新见解，并提示了针对骨质疏松等衰老相关疾病的潜在治疗策略。
